assessments.reasoning: The publisher PDF cover and Introduction pin the June 2024 fifteenth edition and its language name. Section 1 characterizes the ECMAScript 2024 language as general-purpose. Sections 4.1 and 4.2 place browser and server facilities at the host boundary. The archive links the printed and normative forms of the same edition.

challenge.method: Compare the PDF cover, Introduction, §1 and §§4.1–4.2 with the edition listing, and test whether historical names, hosts, later editions or the corrigendum widen or displace the stated identity.
challenge.results: The descriptive naming and language classification agree at the stated edition. The browser and server examples depend on hosts. The archive lists later editions alongside the 2024 edition, and Corrigendum 1 replaces the copyright notice only. The index lifecycle label is a catalog convention.

limitations: The official PDF and HTML share one publisher lineage. The source does not supply the index lifecycle label.
